title: ReIFE: Re-evaluating Instruction-Following Evaluation

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3 LLM-Evaluator Settings (greedy decoding); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all: 1,030 pairs (100 / 319 / 200 / 411) x 2 presentation orders = 2,060 rows built by the hook
task.approximation: none beyond API nondeterminism under greedy decoding

items.config_or_split: src / llmbar_natural, llmbar_adversarial, mtbench, instrusum (files src_*.json)

fields_prose.label: gold '<a|b>|<dataset>' (hook): human winner mapped to the presented order

prompt.system: You are a helpful assistant in evaluating the quality of the outputs for a given instruction. Your goal is to select the best output for the given instruction.
prompt.user_template:
Select the Output (a) or Output (b) that is better for the given instruction. The two outputs are generated by two different AI chatbots respectively.
Here are some rules of the evaluation:
(1) You should prioritize evaluating whether the output honestly/precisely/closely executes the instruction, then consider its helpfulness, accuracy, level of detail, harmlessness, etc.
(2) Outputs should NOT contain more/less than what the instruction asks for, as such outputs do NOT precisely execute the instruction.
(3) You should avoid any potential bias and your judgment should be as objective as possible. For example, the order in which the outputs were presented should NOT affect your judgment, as Output (a) and Output (b) are equally likely to be the better.
Do NOT provide any explanation for your choice.
Do NOT say both / neither are good.
You should answer using ONLY "Output (a)" or "Output (b)". Do NOT output any other words.
# Instruction:
{INSTRUCTION}
# Output (a):
{OUTPUT_1}
# Output (b):
{OUTPUT_2}
# Which is better, Output (a) or Output (b)? Your response should be either "Output (a)" or "Output (b)":

placeholders.OUTPUT_1: items.o1 (output_1 in the 'ab' row, output_2 in the 'ba' row)

prompt.source_location: Appendix C.1, Figure 6 (prompt for the base protocol)

output.postprocess: strip; a reply that does not contain exactly one of the two strings counts as incorrect for that direction

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: hook: accuracy per dataset over both presentation orders, then the unweighted mean over the four datasets (Table 2 Avg.); per-item values reweighted so their mean equals the macro average

notes: InstruSum instructions average 1,150 words, so those 411 pairs dominate cost (~$0.01 per call); the other datasets are short. || [hooks_2 2026-09-07] swapped-order expansion and per-dataset macro average in the hook; prepare verified (2,060 rows x 3 seeds).
hook: harness/tierb/hooks/W4411119263.py: load_items (src splits, both orders), render (Figure 6 prompt), parse (Output (a)/(b), both/neither -> None), score (macro over datasets)
